questions.question: Using the given pie chart (a batsman's 149 runs), prepare an Excel sheet to calculate: (a) how many runs came from ones, twos, fours and sixes, (b) the strike rate of the player, and (c) prepare a pie chart of the shares.
questions.answer:
Data taken from the given chart: ones = 21 balls scoring 1 each, twos = 7 balls, fours = 14 balls, sixes = 9 balls; total runs = 149; balls faced (BF) = 64.

Steps in Excel:
1. Create columns: Type (1s/2s/4s/6s), Balls, Runs = Balls × value.
  • 1s: 21 balls × 1 = 21 runs
  • 2s: 7 balls × 2 = 14 runs
  • 4s: 14 balls × 4 = 56 runs
  • 6s: 9 balls × 6 = 54 runs
  Total = 21 + 14 + 56 + 54 = 145 runs (the chart also mentions other scoring).
2. Strike rate = (Total runs / Balls faced) × 100 = (149 / 64) × 100 ≈ 232.8.
3. Select the Runs column → Insert → Pie Chart to show the share of each type of scoring.
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet makes it easy to calculate totals and percentages and to draw a pie chart from the results.

questions.question: Create a spreadsheet of employees' payroll in MS Excel (Emp ID, Emp Name, Dept, Basic Pay, Medical Allowance, Conveyance Allowance, House Rent, Gross Salary, Income Tax, Net Salary).

• Net Salary = Gross Salary − Income Tax → =F2−G2

Steps: enter the headings in row 1, fill the Emp ID, Name, Dept and Basic Pay, then type the formulas in the first data row and copy them down using the fill handle so that all other rows are calculated automatically.

questions.question: List the properties of a good communication system. Explain any one.
questions.answer:
Properties of a good communication system:
1. Delivery — data must reach the correct destination and user.
2. Accuracy — data must be delivered without errors.
3. Reliability — the system must work consistently.
4. Timeliness — data must arrive on time.
5. Jitter control — variation in delay must be kept within limits.

• Accuracy: the system must deliver the data exactly as it was sent. If the received data differs from the sent data (because of noise, distortion or attenuation), the communication is inaccurate and the information becomes useless or dangerous.
questions.explanation: These properties are the basic requirements of effective data communication.

questions.question: Explain components of communication using single example.
questions.answer:
A communication system has five components: message, sender, receiver, transmission medium and protocol.

Example — sending an email:
• Message: the text of the email.
• Sender: the person who writes and sends the email.
• Receiver: the person who receives the email.
• Transmission medium: the Internet (cables and network equipment).
• Protocol: SMTP, the set of rules that governs how the email is sent.
questions.explanation: All five components must be present for any data communication to take place.

questions.question: Write the function of following network devices: Amplifiers, Routers, Switch, Hub.
questions.answer:
• Amplifier: strengthens (amplifies) a weak signal so that it can travel a longer distance without losing strength.
• Router: connects different networks and finds the best (optimal) path to forward data packets to their destination.
• Switch: connects multiple devices in a LAN and sends data only to the intended device (it is intelligent and uses MAC addresses).
• Hub: a simple device that connects several devices and broadcasts data to all of them (it is non-intelligent).
questions.explanation: A hub broadcasts to everyone while a switch sends data only to the correct device, which makes a switch more efficient.

questions.question: List the causes of signal impairments. Explain any one.
questions.answer:
Causes of signal impairment:
1. Attenuation — loss of signal strength.
2. Distortion — change in the shape of the signal.
3. Noise — unwanted energy added to the signal.

• Attenuation: as a signal travels through the medium it gradually loses energy and becomes weak. This is why signals cannot travel unlimited distances and must be boosted using amplifiers or repeaters.
questions.explanation: Impairment reduces the quality and accuracy of the received signal.

questions.question: What is the difference between radio wave and microwave?
questions.answer:
• Radio waves: lower-frequency electromagnetic waves; omni-directional (spread out in all directions); can pass through walls and buildings; used for AM/FM radio, TV and mobile communication.
• Microwaves: higher-frequency electromagnetic waves; unidirectional (require a line-of-sight path); cannot penetrate solid obstacles; used for satellite links, Wi-Fi and radar.
questions.explanation: Because microwaves need a clear line of sight, microwave towers and satellite dishes must be placed high and aligned.

questions.question: Why OSI model is broken up in layers?
questions.answer:
The OSI model is divided into layers so that a complex networking task is broken into smaller, manageable parts. Each layer performs a specific, well-defined function and communicates with the layers above and below through standard interfaces.

Benefits: simpler design; easy troubleshooting and modification of one layer without affecting the others; interoperability between products from different manufacturers; and easier standardisation and learning.
questions.explanation: The seven OSI layers are Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation and Application.

questions.question: Explain the purpose of Standard Organization.
questions.answer:
Standard organisations develop and publish common rules, formats and protocols for networking and communication so that hardware and software from different manufacturers can work together (interoperability).

Examples: IEEE, IETF, ITU and ANSI. Their standards ensure compatibility, reliability and worldwide communication.
questions.explanation: Without standards, devices from different companies could not communicate with each other.

questions.question: List one merit and one demerit of each topology.
questions.answer:
• Bus: merit — simple and cheap to install; demerit — if the main backbone cable breaks, the whole network fails.
• Star: merit — easy to add/remove devices and one fault affects only one device; demerit — needs more cable and a central hub/switch, and if the hub fails the whole network stops.
• Ring: merit — no collisions, data moves in an orderly way; demerit — failure of one node or cable can break the whole ring.
• Tree: merit — easy to expand into hierarchical groups; demerit — complex, and failure of the backbone/root affects large parts of the network.
questions.explanation: The choice of topology depends on cost, size and reliability requirements of the network.

questions.question: Give one example of LAN, WAN and MAN.
questions.answer:
• LAN (Local Area Network): a network within a school computer lab or an office building.
• MAN (Metropolitan Area Network): a city-wide network, such as a cable-TV network or a network linking several offices across a city.
• WAN (Wide Area Network): the Internet, or a bank's network connecting its branches all over the country (or across continents).
questions.explanation: LAN < MAN < WAN in terms of geographical area covered.

questions.question: How can we measure bit rate and baud rate? Give an example of each.
questions.answer:
• Bit rate: the number of bits transmitted per second, measured in bits per second (bps).
• Baud rate: the number of signal units (symbols) transmitted per second.
Relationship: Bit rate = Baud rate × number of bits per signal unit.

Example: if a line transmits 2400 symbols per second and each symbol carries 1 bit, both the baud rate and the bit rate are 2400. If each symbol carries 4 bits at 1000 symbols/second, the baud rate is 1000 baud and the bit rate is 4000 bps.
questions.explanation: Bit rate measures the actual data speed, while baud rate measures how fast the signal changes.

questions.question: Match the columns: (i) Parts of an IPV4 address

questions.explanation: This mnemonic is a memory aid to remember the order of the OSI layers from top to bottom.

questions.question: Compare Coaxial Cable, UTP, STP and Fiber Optic cable in terms of cost, data rate, installation, interference and maximum length of segment.
questions.answer:
Comparison:
• Coaxial cable — Cost: moderate; Data rate: moderate; Installation: fairly easy; Interference: moderate (shielding helps); Max length: longer than twisted pair (hundreds of metres).
• UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair) — Cost: lowest; Data rate: low–moderate; Installation: easiest; Interference: high (no shielding); Max length: about 100 m.
• STP (Shielded Twisted Pair) — Cost: higher than UTP; Data rate: moderate; Installation: harder (shielding); Interference: low (shielded); Max length: about 100 m.
• Fiber Optic — Cost: highest; Data rate: very high; Installation: difficult (needs skilled work); Interference: none (immune to EMI); Max length: very long (kilometres).
questions.explanation: Fibre optic gives the best speed and immunity but costs the most; UTP is the cheapest but shortest in range.

questions.question: Identify different type of layers of coaxial cable.
questions.answer:
A coaxial cable has four layers (from inside to outside):
1. Inner conductor — a copper wire that carries the signal.
2. Insulation (dielectric) — separates the inner conductor from the shield.
3. Metallic shield (braided mesh/foil) — protects the signal from interference and forms the outer conductor.
4. Outer jacket — a plastic covering that protects the whole cable.
questions.explanation: The shielding of a coaxial cable makes it less prone to interference than twisted pair cable.

questions.question: Make a list of hardware equipment for each topology.
questions.answer:
• Bus topology: one main backbone cable (coaxial), terminators at both ends, network interface cards (NICs) and T-connectors.

• Ring topology: cables connecting each computer in a loop, NICs and (in some types) a token/Multistation Access Unit.
• Tree topology: a backbone cable, hubs/switches at different levels, connectors and NICs.
questions.explanation: Each topology needs different connecting devices and cabling arrangements.

questions.explanation: A hybrid topology is a combination of two or more basic topologies and is used in large networks for flexibility and reliability.

questions.question: Why is computer security important? Write any three reasons.
questions.answer:
Computer security is important because:
1. It protects valuable data and information from theft, loss or damage.
2. It prevents unauthorised access to our computer, accounts and network.
3. It protects our privacy and financial information (passwords, banking details) and keeps the system free from viruses and malware so that work can continue safely.
questions.explanation: Without security, personal and business information can be stolen or destroyed.

questions.question: Explain Cyber Bullying with an example.
questions.answer:
Cyber bullying (cyber harassment) is the use of electronic means such as computers, mobile phones or the Internet to threaten, insult, embarrass or harass a person.

Example: a student repeatedly posts insulting comments and spreads rumours about a classmate on social media, or sends threatening messages to that person.
questions.explanation: Cyber bullying harms the victim's self-esteem and emotions and is a punishable cyber crime.

questions.question: Why is information accuracy important?
questions.answer: Information accuracy is important because decisions, reports, banking, medical treatment and business all depend on correct data. If information is inaccurate it can lead to wrong decisions, financial loss, health risks and loss of trust. In computing, errors can spread very quickly, so data must be verified and kept accurate.
questions.explanation: Accurate information is the basis of reliable decisions and trustworthy systems.

questions.question: What is Ethical Hacking?
questions.answer: Ethical hacking is the practice of testing a computer system or network with the owner's permission, using the same techniques as hackers, in order to find security weaknesses and fix them before criminals can exploit them. Ethical hackers (white-hat hackers) work legally to improve security and protect data.
questions.explanation: Ethical hacking is done with consent and for protection, whereas criminal hacking is done illegally and for harm or profit.

questions.question: Your friend has become a victim of cyber harassment. What two advices will you give him or her?
questions.answer:
Two advices:
1. Do not reply or react to the harasser, and do not delete the evidence — save copies/screenshots of the messages.
2. Report the incident to a trusted adult (parents/teacher) and to the authorities/website — block the person, report the account, and in Pakistan contact the National Response Centre for Cyber Crimes helpline 9911.
questions.explanation: Staying calm, preserving evidence and reporting are the safest ways to deal with cyber harassment.

questions.question: Write any two measures to avoid email account hacking.
questions.answer:
Two measures:
1. Use a strong, unique password, keep it secret, change it regularly and enable two-step verification.
2. Never open suspicious links or attachments or give your password on unknown websites, and always log out from public/shared computers.
questions.explanation: Most email hacking is caused by weak passwords and by giving away login details on fake (phishing) pages.

questions.question: How is software piracy harmful for software developers?
questions.answer: Software piracy (the illegal use, copying or distribution of software) harms developers because they lose the sales revenue and profit they should have earned. This reduces the money available for research, updates, customer support and employees' salaries, discourages innovation, and can force companies to raise prices for honest customers.
questions.explanation: Piracy is both illegal and unethical as it violates the creator's copyright.

questions.question: Give two examples of phishing.
questions.answer:
Two examples:
1. A fake email pretending to be from a bank that asks you to click a link and confirm your account details.
2. A fraudulent website or message posing as a trusted company that asks for your username, password or credit-card details.
questions.explanation: Phishing uses false emails/websites to trick people into giving sensitive information.

questions.question: What is an Intellectual Property Right?
questions.answer: Intellectual Property Right (IPR) is a legal right that protects the creations of the human intellect — such as inventions, literary and artistic works, software, designs, symbols and names. IPR prevents others from stealing or illegally using these creations and is enforced through copyrights, patents and trademarks.
questions.explanation: IPR encourages creativity and innovation by giving creators control over their work.

questions.question: Differentiate the following on the given criteria: Virus, Worm, Adware, Spyware.
questions.answer:
Criteria: (1) How is it initiated? (2) Means to spread (3) Effect on computer speed (4) Damage to data/hardware (5) Level of danger.

• Virus — initiated when an infected file/program is run; spreads through infected files, email attachments and USB devices; slows the computer; can corrupt or delete data and damage software; danger: high.
• Worm — initiates and runs by itself (no host file needed); spreads automatically across networks/email; consumes network bandwidth and slows the computer; can delete files and overload networks; danger: high.
• Adware — comes with free/downloaded software; spreads through downloads and pop-up ads; slows browsing/computer slightly; shows unwanted ads and redirects the browser; danger: low (least harmful).
• Spyware — installed secretly along with other software; spreads with bundled downloads; may slow the computer; secretly steals personal data and passwords; danger: high.
questions.explanation: All four are types of malware, but they differ in how they start, spread and harm the system.

questions.question: During classroom discussion, put the following situations before students and discuss what they will do and why: (a) a phone call claiming you won a prize but asking an advance payment; (b) a file from an unknown email asking your bank details or email ID and password; (c) a website demanding your Facebook/Gmail credentials to view content.

questions.explanation: The rule is: never share personal or financial information with unknown persons, links or websites.

questions.explanation: Planning and testing before publishing help avoid mistakes and give a professional result.

questions.question: Is it possible to display the entire contents of another web page in our HTML page? How?

questions.explanation: A String (text) data type is used to store text such as names. Integer and Float store numbers, and Boolean stores True/False.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Integer  (b) Float  (c) String  (d) Boolean

questions.question: A key that allows only unique entries in a field is called:
questions.answer: (a) Primary Key
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a table, so it allows only unique values (no duplicates and no nulls).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Primary Key  (b) Secondary Key  (c) Foreign Key  (d) Super Key

questions.question: Data Redundancy means:
questions.answer: (a) Duplication of Data
questions.explanation: Data redundancy means the unnecessary duplication (repetition) of the same data in more than one place. A good database design reduces redundancy.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Duplication of Data  (b) Variety of Data  (c) Size of Data  (d) Data Type

questions.question: The relationship that matches one record of an entity with only one record of another entity is called:
questions.answer: (a) One-to-One relationship
questions.explanation: In a one-to-one relationship, one record of an entity is related to only one record of another entity (e.g., one person has one national ID card).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) One-to-One relationship  (b) One-to-Many relationship  (c) Many-to-One relationship  (d) Many-to-Many relationship

questions.question: The shape that is used to represent an attribute in an ERD is:
questions.answer: (d) An ellipse
questions.explanation: In an Entity Relationship Diagram, an entity is drawn as a rectangle, an attribute as an ellipse (oval) and a relationship as a diamond.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) A diamond  (b) An octagon  (c) A rectangle  (d) An ellipse

questions.question: Why Database Management System is preferred over Flat File System?
questions.explanation: A flat file stores everything in one file, causing duplication and difficulty in managing and updating data.

questions.question: Discuss the use of databases in business with example.
questions.answer:
Databases are used in business to store and manage large amounts of related data such as customers, products, sales and employees.

Example: a bank stores customer accounts, balances and transactions in a database; using it, the bank can quickly find a customer's balance, generate statements and detect fraud. Similarly, a school keeps student records, marks and attendance in a database.
questions.explanation: A database lets a business retrieve accurate information quickly and make better decisions.

questions.question: What is the difference between Design View and Datasheet View?
questions.answer:
• Design View: used to define or change the structure of a table — the field names, data types, descriptions and the primary key.
• Datasheet View: used to enter, view and edit the actual data (records) of the table in a row-and-column layout, similar to a spreadsheet.
questions.explanation: Design View defines the table's structure, while Datasheet View is used for the data itself.

questions.question: Why is it important to carefully decide the data type for each field?
questions.explanation: For example, a phone number should be stored as text, but marks should be stored as numbers.

questions.question: What is the difference between table and view?
questions.answer:
• Table: a stored object in the database that physically holds the data in rows (records) and columns (fields).
• View: a virtual table — it does not store data itself; it shows data selected from one or more tables by a query.

A view is used to display only the required data and to hide sensitive fields from certain users.
questions.explanation: A view acts like a window into the data of one or more tables.

questions.question: Explain entities, attributes and relationships with one example of each.
questions.answer:
• Entity: a real-world object or person about which data is stored (e.g., Student, Teacher).
• Attribute: a property or characteristic of an entity (e.g., Roll No, Name, Address of a Student).
• Relationship: an association between two entities (e.g., a Student is enrolled in a Class).

Example: Entity = Student; its attributes = Roll No, Name, Class; relationship = Student → enrolled in → Class.
questions.explanation: In an ERD, entities are rectangles, attributes are ellipses and relationships are diamonds.

questions.question: List the major characteristics of primary and foreign keys.
questions.answer:
• Primary key: uniquely identifies each record in a table; it never contains duplicate values and cannot be null; a table has only one primary key.
• Foreign key: a field in one table that refers to the primary key of another table; it may contain duplicate values and may be null; it is used to create a link (relationship) between two tables and to maintain referential integrity.
questions.explanation: Primary key = unique identifier of a table; foreign key = reference to another table's primary key.

questions.question: Write three benefits of using relationships in the database.
questions.answer:
Three benefits:
1. They avoid data redundancy, because data is not repeated in every table.
2. They maintain data integrity and consistency, since related data is stored once and linked.
3. They make it easy to combine and retrieve data from several tables through queries and reports.
questions.explanation: Relationships are the basis of a well-designed relational database.

questions.question: Discuss the importance of ERD in business.
questions.explanation: A good ERD saves time and cost by planning the database properly before implementation.

questions.question: Write any two statements from the following ER Diagram (Company – Advertisement – Candidate – Interview).
questions.answer:
Two statements from the ER diagram:
1. A Company releases an Advertisement (Company → releases → Advertisement).
2. A Candidate applies for an Advertisement and faces an Interview (Candidate → applies for → Advertisement; Candidate → faces → Interview).

Other statements: a Candidate takes/appears in an Interview; an Advertisement brings Candidates.
questions.explanation: An ER diagram can be read as simple sentences describing how the entities are related.

questions.answer: (b) Always unique value in field
questions.explanation: A primary key always holds a unique value in its field so that each record can be identified.

questions.question: Match the columns: (ii) Integer data
questions.answer: (d) Number without decimal point
questions.explanation: Integer data type stores whole numbers (numbers without a decimal point).

questions.answer: (e) Connection between two tables

questions.explanation: A view is a virtual table that shows data selected from one or more tables without storing it.

questions.explanation: An entity becomes a table that has its own attributes (fields).

questions.question: Create few tables and practice adding, updating and deleting records in MS Access.
questions.answer:
Steps:
1. Open MS Access and create a Blank Database.
2. Create → Table Design; add fields (e.g., Roll No, Name, Marks) with their data types and set a primary key.
3. Switch to Datasheet View.
• Adding: type new data in the last empty row.
• Updating: click in a cell and change its value.
• Deleting: select the row (record) and press Delete (confirm the warning).
4. Save the table with a suitable name.
questions.explanation: These operations practise data entry (CRUD) in a database table.

questions.question: Create a table in MS Access by importing an Excel Sheet. Examine the data type of each field after importing and change where required.
questions.answer:
Steps:
1. External Data → New Data Source → From File → Excel.
2. Browse to the Excel file, choose "Import the source data into a new table" and select the sheet.
3. Tick "First Row Contains Column Headings" and click Next/Finish.
4. Open the new table in Design View.
5. Check the data type of each field (text, number, date, etc.) and change any field whose type was detected wrongly, then save.
questions.explanation: Access guesses the data types from the data, so the types should always be checked after importing.

questions.question: Create different views to show data from two tables.
questions.answer:
Steps:
1. Make sure the two tables have a common field (related by a foreign key).
2. Create → Query Design; add both tables to the query window.
3. Join the common fields (Access shows a line between them).
4. Select the fields you want to display from the two tables in the grid.
5. Run the query to see the combined data, and save it as a view/query (e.g., "StudentMarks").
questions.explanation: A query (view) combines data from two tables without storing a duplicate copy.

questions.question: Draw a simple ERD on paper and implement it in MS Access (at least three entities, attributes, data types, primary and foreign keys and simple relationships).
questions.answer:
Task guidance:
1. Choose three entities, e.g., Student, Class and Teacher.
2. List attributes for each (Student: RollNo, Name, ClassID; Class: ClassID, ClassName; Teacher: TeacherID, Name, ClassID).
3. Draw rectangles for entities, ellipses for attributes and diamonds for relationships; mark primary keys (underlined).
4. Implement in Access: create a table for each entity in Design View, set the correct data type for every field and set the primary key.
5. Add foreign-key fields and create relationships using Database Tools → Relationships (drag the primary key of one table onto the matching field of another).
questions.explanation: This activity brings together all the database concepts: entities, attributes, data types, keys and relationships.
